definition: The Berndt–Hall–Hall–Hausman (BHHH) algorithm is a numerical optimization algorithm similar to the Newton–Raphson algorithm, but it replaces the observed negative Hessian matrix with the outer product of the gradient.
details: This approximation is based on the information matrix equality and therefore only valid while maximizing a likelihood function. The BHHH algorithm is named after the four originators: Ernst R. Berndt, Bronwyn Hall, Robert Hall, and Jerry Hausman.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. In plain words: The Berndt–Hall–Hall–Hausman (BHHH) algorithm is a numerical optimization algorithm similar to the Newton–Raphson algorithm, but it replaces the observed negative Hessian matrix with the outer product of the gradient. Here is how it actually plays out: This approximation is based on the information matrix equality and therefore only valid while maximizing a likelihood function. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Berndt–Hall–Hall–Hausman algorithm.
